newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE and MGE to study durum wheat futures contract.
newsitem.headline: WCE and MGE to study durum wheat futures contract.

text.p: The Winnipeg Commodity Exchange and the Minneapolis Grain Exchange said on Friday they will study the potential for a North American durum wheat futures contract, a WCE statement said.
There is no futures contract in durum wheat anywhere in the world. World durum trade is about 6.0 million tonnes.

"North American durum exports represent 90 percent of the world trade and future prospects for growth are excellent. There is enough price volatility in global durum trade suggesting a need for a mechanism to manage this price risk," WCE chairman Terry James said.

The Canada-U.S. border is the center of the North American durum wheat growing region and an area where both exchanges provide risk management products for agricultural commodities, the WCE statement said.

"To compete in the world marketplace today, there is a need to use the critical mass of production from both countries to support a viable contract," MGE president and chief executive James Lindau said.
About half of world durum exports are sold to the North African market. The Canadian Wheat Board held a 71 percent share of the world market in crop year 1994/95 (Aug/July).
